title: Deep Impact on Comet Tempel 1
gravity_note: Tempel 1's gravity is roughly 1/25,000 of Earth's. Escape speed is only about 1.5 m/s, a brisk walk: jump and you are gone.

height.product: Plate shape model of comet 9P/Tempel 1 v2.0 (Thomas et al. 2013; 16,022 vertices), DIF-C-HRIV/ITS/MRI-5-TEMPEL1-SHAPE-V2.0
height.credit: P. Thomas et al. / NASA Deep Impact and Stardust-NExT; PDS Small Bodies Node

color.product: Shaded relief rendered from the same shape model
color.credit: Derived from the Thomas et al. 2013 Tempel 1 shape model (NASA)

note: Impact site (2005-07-04) at about 28 S, 16 E in the Thomas et al. (2013) model frame, as converted by Nagdimunov et al. 2014 (arXiv:1406.3308). The site is approximate, uncertain by a few hundred metres, because ejecta hid it from the shape-model control points. The ~50 m crater that Stardust-NExT saw in 2011 is NOT in the model. The shape model has a vertex spacing of about 90 m, so this patch is a smooth, low-detail surface interpolated onto a 3.9 m grid. "Up" = best-fit plane normal within 500 m; "north" = spin axis projected onto that plane. Colour is shaded relief rendered from the shape model (sun from the north-west), not a photograph; the shape model has no albedo, so brightness only shows slopes. Heights smoothed with a 40 m Gaussian to hide plate facets.
